intent: Frame one text field and its addons (icons, text, compact actions) as a single visually unified field.
typical_uses: A field with a fixed text prefix or suffix (a currency sign, a domain, a unit)
A field with several adornments on one side, or an icon on one side and an action on the other
A multi-line field with a full-width addon row above or below it

dont_use_when.situation: A single decorative leading icon or one compact trailing action on a single-line field

instead.note: Input's own `icon` and `end` slots cover this without the extra parts.

dont_use_when.situation: Joining independent controls that are not one logical field (a segmented control, a split button, an input beside a popup trigger)
A caption, description or error message for the field

instead.note: InputGroup draws only the field's frame; the label, helper text and error sit beside it in a Field, wired to the control by hand.

invariants.text: The group draws the field's border, background, focus ring and error border; a wrapped InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea has its own border, background, radius and ring removed by input-group.module.css and fills the row.

The group's states come from the wrapped control, never from the group: its focus ring shows while an InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea inside it matches `:focus-visible` (a focused button in an addon does not light it), `aria-invalid="true"` on that control turns the group border destructive, and a disabled control dims the whole group once. `aria-invalid` or `disabled` set on InputGroup itself changes nothing.
`size` sets the group's minimum height and its addon inset, gap and direct-icon box; a block-start or block-end addon or a wrapped InputGroupTextarea grows the group past that floor.

The group renders a div with `role="group"` and no accessible name of its own; an `aria-label` given to InputGroup names that group, not the field, so the field's own name goes on InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea.

anti_patterns.dont: Put two text fields in one InputGroup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give each field its own InputGroup; one group frames one field with one focus ring and one error border

a11y.by: input-group.test.tsx asserts the group resolves by getByRole('group'), and that an aria-label passed to InputGroup names it (getByRole('group', { name: 'Amount field' }))

good.title: Search field with a leading icon and a trailing clear action
good.code:
<InputGroup size="sm">
  <InputGroupAddon>
    <SearchIcon />
  </InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput type="search" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton icon={<XIcon />} aria-label="Clear" onClick={clear} />
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>

bad.title: Error state set on the group
bad.why: The group keys its destructive border off the wrapped control's `aria-invalid`, and on a div the attribute means nothing to assistive tech either; put `aria-invalid` on InputGroupInput.
